'''''Libertia chilensis''''', [[Synonym (taxonomy)|synonym]] '''''Libertia formosa''''',<ref name=POWO_439844-1/> called the '''New Zealand satin flower''',<ref name=RHS/> '''snowy mermaid''',<ref>{{PLANTS|id=LIFO|taxon=Libertia formosa|accessdate= 2 June 2015}}</ref> or '''Chilean-iris''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007|accessdate=2014-10-17}}</ref> is a species of flowering plant in the iris [[Family (taxonomy)|family]], [[Iridaceae]], native to the [[Juan Fernández Islands]], [[Central Chile|central]] and southern Chile, and southern Argentina.<ref name=POWO_439844-1/> It can also be found growing wild in the [[San Francisco Bay Area]] and [[San Bernardino County, California|San Bernardino County]] in [[California]],<ref name=BONAP>{{BONAP|ref|genus=Libertia|species=formosa|accessdate=20 April 2019}}</ref> where it is an [[introduced species]]. A [[rhizome|rhizomatous]] [[evergreen]] [[perennial plant|perennial]], it has gained the [[Royal Horticultural Society]]'s [[Award of Garden Merit]].<ref name=RHS>{{cite web |title=''Libertia chilensis'' New Zealand satin flower |url=https://www.rhs.org.uk/Plants/23471/Libertia-chilensis/Details |publisher=The Royal Horticultural Society |access-date=14 March 2021 }}</ref>

The [[Calle-Calle River]] in [[Los Ríos Region]] owes its name to the [[Mapuche language|Mapuche]] word for the plant.<ref name=museoniebla>{{Cite web|url=https://www.museodeniebla.gob.cl/643/w3-propertyvalue-42964.html?_noredirect=1|title=Historia|access-date=2021-04-01|website=Museo de Sitio Castillo de Niebla|publisher=Servicio Nacional del Patrimonio Cultural|language=es|archive-date=2020-08-04|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200804005645/https://www.museodeniebla.gob.cl/643/w3-propertyvalue-42964.html?_noredirect=1|url-status=dead}}</ref>
